penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Each MBOX-to-IMAP migration is a per-client technical job: validating the source archive, running the migration tool, verifying integrity, and troubleshooting failures — a human or at minimum a managed server process per customer.

rationale: The buyer is reasonably clear — MSPs and IT managers at SMBs who repeatedly handle email migrations and do pay for tools — and willingness to pay is moderate (existing paid tools like Aid4Mail exist). However, the actual migration work cannot be automated by Claude: it requires ingesting potentially gigabytes of MBOX files, running server-side tooling (imapsync etc.), and validating the output — per-customer technical fulfillment that a solo non-technical operator cannot deliver autonomously. The penalty for human fulfillment, combined with low operational autonomy, drops this below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This is not a viable autonomous micro-service for this factory. Each migration requires the customer to upload large files to a server, run migration tooling, and verify results — none of which Claude can do in a hands-off way without significant infrastructure and per-job human oversight. A written guide product (paid PDF/course) is possible but would earn very little. The honest assessment is that a managed migration service is a technical services business requiring infrastructure and hands-on work per client — not a Claude-automated product. Dropping this candidate is correct.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (4 < 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (5 < 6). The product that could exist here (a polished MBOX migration SaaS) would require real infrastructure engineering, not a prompt + Stripe link.
